inputs.sbc_source: Annual securities report FYE 2026-03-31 (4523.T_Annual_FY2025_SecuritiesReportSummary.txt:10914 and the FY2025 statement of changes in equity): share-based payments ¥121m (prior years ¥145m, ¥312m). Restricted-stock scheme for directors only; 0.015% of revenue, so projected at 0% (SBC-zero market) and kept as an explicit zero row.
inputs.fy_label_note: CSV/period labels are END-year: 'FY2026' here is the year ended 2026-03-31, which Eisai itself calls 'FY2025'. Guidance quoted by the company for 'FY2026' (Apr-2026 to Mar-2027) is projection year 1 (CSV FY2027). The company's FY2028 medium-term targets land in projection year 3.
inputs.share_count_basis: 281,890,450 shares outstanding net of treasury at 2026-06-30 (Q1 FY2026 tanshin p.2). No dilutive securities: diluted EPS is printed as '-' in every filing. Held FLAT; SBC is immaterial and expensed. The ¥30.1bn buyback in the year to Mar-2025 took the count from 286.8m to 283.5m; only ¥9m was repurchased in the year to Mar-2026 and nil in Q1, so the flat count is a convention, not a funded programme.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Bonds and borrowings only (current ¥86,738m + non-current ¥184,604m = ¥271,342m at 2026-06-30, after the June-2026 ¥50bn straight-bond issue under the ¥300bn shelf) less cash and cash equivalents ¥311,739m. Lease liabilities (¥43,070m at 2026-03-31, inside 'other financial liabilities') are EXCLUDED because the lease cash cost is charged in the flows (treatment B).
inputs.owner_fcf_fy0_note: last_fcf = 20,156 reported FCF (OCF 61,323 - PPE capex 15,359 - intangibles 25,808) - SBC 121 - interest income 7,964 = 12,071. After the lease cash the engine charges in the flows (principal 10,432 + interest 1,201), FY0 owner FCF was ~¥0.4bn: the company generated essentially no free cash in the year to Mar-2026 and negative owner FCF in the two years before (Leqembi launch spend, European restructuring, ¥25.8bn of in-licensing). The forward build therefore starts from components anchored to FY2026 guidance (operating profit ¥70bn), not from a trailing margin.
inputs.interest_income_note: Financial income ¥12,196m = interest on amortised-cost assets 7,964 + retirement-benefit-asset interest 319 + dividends 453 + a one-off ¥3,460m gain on sale/valuation of financial assets. Only the 7,964 is stripped from last_fcf (the rest never enters EBITDA-based projections). Matching assets: cash is in net debt; the ¥39,809m FVTOCI equity-securities portfolio is added in equity_bridge.
inputs.capex_normalisation: Capex in core_metrics = PPE purchases + intangible-asset purchases (in-licensing upfronts/milestones, product rights). Intangibles are lumpy: ¥33.3bn (FY2016), 12.2, 14.2, 9.5, 35.0, 19.0, 11.4, 12.0, 10.5, 11.0, 25.8bn (FY2026, taletrectinib + serplulimab); 10-year mean ¥17.6bn. PPE runs ¥12-23bn. In-licensing is a genuine recurring cost of pipeline replenishment for a pharma facing a 2030 Lenvima cliff, so it is NOT stripped; capex is modelled at 4.3% of revenue (10-yr blended mean 4.9%, 5-yr 4.3%; ~1.8pp PPE + ~2.5pp intangibles) easing to 4.0% as the Leqembi SC and BBM infrastructure matures. D&A is charged ex right-of-use depreciation (reported ¥39,550m less ~¥10bn ROU, estimated from the ¥10.4bn lease principal) at 3.6% of revenue easing to 3.4%, so leases are charged once.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY, the currency of the statements and flows. 10-year JGB ~1.7% (Oct-2026) + beta 1.0 x JPY ERP 5.5% = cost of equity ~7.2%; after-tax cost of the new straight bonds ~0.8%; ~15% debt weight on the post-shelf capital structure gives ~6.2%, rounded to 6.5%. Same WACC in every scenario: Leqembi competitive/safety risk and the Lenvima patent cliff are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate (adaptations rule f). Terminal growth 1.5% (JPY nominal; a patent-churn business should not be capitalised at GDP+), and the terminal cap is 15x FCF rather than 20x because every product in the portfolio has a finite exclusivity window.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. The full lease payment (principal ¥10,432m + interest ¥1,201m = ¥11,633m, 1.4% of revenue; yuho cash-flow statement and note on financial costs) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities are excluded from net debt; D&A for cash tax is ex-ROU depreciation. Post-IFRS-16 EBITDA (operating profit + D&A = ¥83.7bn in FY2026) is the margin anchor, which is why the lease line must be deducted.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are modelled on a consolidated basis; the non-controlling-interest stock (¥26,606m at 2026-06-30, ~5% of profit, mainly Chinese and Japanese subsidiaries) is deducted once in equity_bridge. Not folded into the tax rate as well.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md row 2: non-US operating company, plus adaptations a1 JPY WACC, b leases, c NCI, d excluded income/matching asset, e SBC-zero). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. Partner structures do not need separate treatment: Eisai books Lenvima and Leqembi revenue gross and expenses the Merck profit share (¥158.2bn in FY2026) and Biogen's Leqembi share inside cost of sales/SG&A, so the alliances show up as a structurally lower EBITDA margin (10-13% today vs 15-18% pre-Leqembi), which the margin paths carry. Nothing is a royalty stream that would need capitalising separately. Cash tax: taxes paid ¥16.7bn on PBT ¥51.0bn (33%) in FY2026 and ¥20.2bn on ¥61.1bn (33%) in FY2025 vs a 20% P&L effective rate; modelled at 28% of EBIT as a blend of Japan 30.6%, US ~25% and China/Asia 15-25% on the geographic profit mix. Working capital: receivables + inventory exceed payables (pharma distributor profile), so growth consumes cash: wc_capture_pct -10. Street/house band collapses (SBC-zero): band_position should be read as n/a. 10-year horizon because margins are still ramping AND the Lenvima US generic entry (July 2030, projection year 5) must sit inside the explicit period rather than inside the terminal value.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (+5.0%) and revenue CAGR (+5.0%) agree, but EPS CAGR is negative over both windows (-10.9% 3yr, -1.4% 5yr) and owner FCF collapsed from ¥22bn (FY2021) to ~¥0.4bn (FY2026, lease-adjusted) with a negative FY2023 (-¥52bn, so the 3-year owner-FCF CAGR is undefined). Revenue grew while profit and cash did not: the Leqembi build-out and partner profit shares absorbed the growth. The book-value CAGR is the least-bad anchor and is used only as a cross-check; the forward path is built from guidance and product-level judgment, not from any of these.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs on CSV end-year labels: FY2021 -> FY2026 (5yr), FY2023 -> FY2026 (3yr). Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - interest income - lease principal and interest. Reported FCF 5yr CAGR -10.8% vs owner -54%: the gap is interest income rising from ¥1.9bn to ¥8.0bn on the cash pile plus ~¥11bn/yr of lease cash, neither of which belongs to operations.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 +7.5% vs guidance +7.0% (Q1 ran +15.6% and Leqembi Q2 prelim ¥32.2bn supports the ¥143.5bn full-year). Y2-Y3 carry revenue to ~¥988bn against the company's ¥1,000bn FY2028 target (CSV FY2029). Y4 slows as legacy erosion offsets; Y5-Y6 (years ending Mar-2031/32) take the Lenvima US generic entry of July 2030: Lenvima falls from ~¥345bn to ~¥200bn over two years while Leqembi reaches ~¥400bn and Dayvigo ~¥100bn, net -2%/yr. Y7-Y10 recover at 2-2.5% on Leqembi maintenance volume, SC initiation and the in-licensed oncology assets.
base.margin_rationale: Y1 12.4% = guided operating profit ¥70bn + D&A ¥39.5bn on ¥887bn. Y3 13.5% gives ~¥94bn operating profit vs the ¥90bn FY2028 target. The Lenvima cliff removes ~¥55-65bn of contribution (revenue less Merck share and COGS) but Leqembi at ¥400bn with ~27% contribution after Biogen's share adds ~¥80bn, so the margin holds ~13.5% through the cliff and reaches 15.5% by Y10, still below the 15.7-17.6% Eisai earned in FY2016-FY2019 before the Leqembi build-out.

bull.narrative: Leqembi becomes a ¥550-600bn franchise by the Lenvima cliff (IQLIK initiation approval, BBM diagnostics halving the diagnostic funnel cost, European reimbursement, China commercial-insurance uptake, AHEAD 3-45 preclinical readout positive in FY2028), the cliff is fully absorbed with revenue still growing, and the margin returns to the pre-launch 17-18% band and beyond as Leqembi's R&D rolls off.

bear.narrative: Leqembi plateaus near ¥200-250bn as Kisunla's once-monthly, stop-when-clear regimen and Lilly's commercial scale take share, an ARIA-related label tightening or litigation slows initiation, ex-US reimbursement stays patchy; the Lenvima cliff then hits an un-replaced top line (-8%, -6%), the Merck profit share no longer shields the margin, in-licensing spend continues at ¥25bn/yr to rebuild the pipeline, and EBITDA margin sits at 10-12%.

scenario_narratives.base: Leqembi delivers the FY2026 guide (¥143.5bn) and compounds to ~¥400bn by the year ending Mar-2031 as the subcutaneous autoinjector moves initiation to the home and blood-based biomarkers widen the diagnosed pool, while Lilly's Kisunla takes a meaningful but not dominant share. Dayvigo grows to ~¥100bn. Lenvima holds ~¥345bn until US generic entry in July 2030, then loses ~40% over two years with the Merck profit share falling in step. The legacy portfolio (Aricept, Fycompa, Halaven, Pariet, Methycobal) erodes 2-3%/yr. Operating profit reaches the ¥90bn FY2028 target a year early, dips through the cliff, and the EBITDA margin settles at 15.5%, short of the pre-Leqembi 16-18% because Biogen and Merck permanently take half the profit on the two largest products. In-licensing (taletrectinib, serplulimab and successors) keeps capex at ~4% of revenue. Cash generation recovers from ~zero today to ¥35bn in year 1 and ~¥75bn by year 10.
scenario_narratives.bull: Leqembi becomes the standard of care for early Alzheimer's: IQLIK initiation approval in the US (PDUFA Aug-2026), BBM-based diagnosis making up over half of confirmations by FY2028, German/UK/Spanish/Italian reimbursement, Chinese commercial-insurance coverage and a positive AHEAD 3-45 readout in preclinical AD take the franchise to ¥550-600bn by the Lenvima cliff and keep it growing in maintenance dosing after. Revenue never falls through the cliff (+1%/yr in years 5-6), EBITDA margin climbs to 19% as Leqembi's trial costs roll off and the European and US structural reforms hold the cost base, and the ¥300bn bond shelf funds in-licensing without dilution. This is the case that justifies the current ~27x forward P/E.
scenario_narratives.bear: Kisunla's convenience and Lilly's scale cap Leqembi at ¥200-250bn, an ARIA safety event or label change slows initiation, and ex-US access stays commercial-insurance-only in China and delayed in Europe. The July-2030 Lenvima generics (Sun, Dr. Reddy's, Torrent) then strip ¥150bn of revenue from a top line with nothing to replace it (-8%, -6% in years 5-6), the EMEA/Japan Lenvima LOE follows, and pipeline replenishment through in-licensing keeps capex at 4%+ of revenue while the EBITDA margin sits at 10-12%. The dividend (¥160, ¥45bn/yr) stays flat and consumes most of free cash; the ¥300bn bond programme becomes the funding source for the next pipeline, and the balance sheet moves from net cash to net debt.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved off the 15/50/35 default to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25%: the thesis rests on a single drug's ramp against a better-resourced direct competitor (Lilly) with a boxed safety warning, on top of a dated patent cliff on the product that is 42% of revenue, and trailing owner FCF is ~zero so there is no cash cushion if the ramp stalls. Bull cut to 25%: it needs IQLIK initiation approval, BBM uptake, European and Chinese reimbursement, a clean safety record and a positive AHEAD 3-45 readout to all land together. Base 50% because FY2026 guidance (+7% revenue, operating profit ¥70bn) is tracking ahead after Q1 and the Leqembi Q2 preliminary (¥32.2bn) is consistent with the full-year guide.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Eisai is valued as a consolidated owner-FCF stream in JPY with the partner profit shares left inside the margin, because that is how the cash actually arrives. Two things dominate: how far Leqembi scales before July 2030, and how much of the Lenvima contribution survives the cliff. The scenarios bracket those two questions; the discount rate does not. Trailing cash generation is near zero, so the valuation is almost entirely a forward margin-recovery story, which is why the explicit horizon runs ten years and the terminal multiple is capped at 15x FCF rather than 20x. At ~27x guided EPS and ~12.5x guided EBITDA the market is paying for something between the base and bull cases; the house base case does not get there.
key_risks_to_valuation: Leqembi share loss to Lilly's Kisunla (monthly IV, time-limited dosing) or an ARIA safety event/label tightening slowing initiation
Lenvima US generic entry July 2030 (settlements with Sun, Dr. Reddy's, Torrent); Shilpa litigation could extend to 2036 for that challenger only, and ex-US LOE follows
Margin capture: Merck (¥158bn/yr) and Biogen profit shares cap the EBITDA margin well below pre-2020 levels even on strong revenue
Owner FCF has been ~zero for three years; the valuation is a forward recovery, not a capitalisation of demonstrated cash
Currency: 71% of revenue is non-JPY; a stronger yen compresses reported revenue and margin, and the JPY-built WACC does not hedge that
Drug-pricing policy (Japan biennial revisions, US MFN/tariff proposals, European reimbursement) and the ¥300bn bond programme shifting the balance sheet from net cash to net debt
Lumpy in-licensing: a large upfront (FY2026 ¥25.8bn) in any year can wipe out that year's free cash
